summary: Polk County, OR lookout on Bald Mountain (listed as Monmouth Bald) from the 1910s; last 40-foot tower removed 1969 or abandoned 1971; now gone.

facts.design: 40-foot timber tower with a 14x14 cab, built 1947 (Forest Lookouts); earlier pole tower (1941) and a 90-foot tower without cab (1942 inspection)
facts.status_note: Register and firelookout.com say abandoned 1971 and now gone; Forest Lookouts says removed 1969

access.note: No source we read describes access to the site or whether the public can reach it

events.note: State report (1914) describes a telephone line to the lookout station on top of Bald Mountain
Polk County Fire Patrol Association instructs its manager to build a new lookout station on top of Bald Mountain
High lookout tower on the summit nearly finished by a crew under W.V. Fuller (June 1918 newspaper report)
Federal wireless receiving outfit installed at the station; in operation under T.C. Stockwell
T.C. Stockwell in charge of the new station as lookout and wireless operator (Statesman Journal, July 4, 1920)
Station at Bald Mountain reported completed (June 17, 1922)
Blaze on the west slope of Bald Mountain in July 1922; Morning Oregonian reported the lookout left his post, and the district warden said he did not
William Caldwell is the lookout at Bald Mountain
June 1925 fire threatens the Cobbs-Mitchell Lumber sawmill and the town of Valsetz; Caldwell reports by telephone
New tower of about 60 feet erected on the spot of an old tower that had decayed
Winter winds blow the 66-foot tower over in December 1933 (reported March 1934); the district warden estimates repairs at slightly over $100
14x16 ground cabin built (per 1942 inspection report on the Forest Lookouts page)
Pole live-in tower built, per Register; replaced by a 40-foot tower
June 1942 inspection report describes a 90-foot tower without a cab, used mainly for fire detection
Lyle Thomas serving as lookout for the fire association at Bald Mountain
40-foot timber tower with 14x14 cab constructed (Forest Lookouts); 40' live-in tower (firelookout.com)
Four first reports made from this station in 1966
Lookout removed (Forest Lookouts). Register and firelookout.com give 1971 for abandonment instead
Tower abandoned; now gone (Register and firelookout.com)
Registered November 11, 2010 as FFLOS US 720, OR 131; nominated by Ray Kresek

corrections.why: 27.4 m is 90 feet, the height a June 1942 inspection gave for a tower without a cab. The Register and firelookout.com describe the later standing tower as 40 feet (about 12.2 m).

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Forest Lookouts history is titled Bald Mountain while the Register and firelookout.com use Monmouth Bald. Both accounts date a 40-foot tower to 1947 and place it in Polk County, so we treat them as one summit. No source says so outright.
The 90-foot figure (1942) and the 40-foot figure (1947 tower) are different towers. The site's last standing tower was 40 feet, per the Register and firelookout.com.

sources.title: Monmouth Bald Lookout Site, Former Fire Lookout Sites Register

notes_for_editor: Identity of the Forest Lookouts 'Bald Mountain' with the register's Monmouth Bald is inferred from the Polk County location and the shared 1947 40-foot tower, not stated in any source. Removal (1969, Forest Lookouts) and abandonment (1971, Register and firelookout.com) dates conflict and are unresolved. The 1942 inspection and 1941 pole tower do not line up cleanly; the 1942 inspection's post is not named on the page, though it sits in the Bald Mountain history. The 1943 memo on that page mentions a 'Monmouth cabin' and Fanno posts, which may be the same station and was not used. Access level is unknown; no source describes the site now or public access. Access to the site was not confirmed. No photos found. Brief's height_m 27.4 corrected to 12.2.
